notes.author: Sleep medicine physician
notes.text:
Polysomnography Report
Date: 04/02/2025
Patient: Elvina Schaden, 68-year-old female

Diagnostic in-laboratory polysomnography performed 04/02/2025. Total apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) 43.9 events/hour. Central and mixed apneas comprised 39% of all events. These results indicate severe sleep apnea with a notable proportion of central and mixed apneas. Clinical evaluation and appropriate treatment are recommended.

notes.title: Sleep Medicine Consultation
notes.author: Sleep medicine physician
notes.text:
Sleep Medicine Consultation
Date: 07/31/2026
Patient: Elvina Schaden, 69-year-old female

Reason for Consultation:
Evaluation and management of sleep-disordered breathing.

History:
Elvina is a 69-year-old female referred for assessment of sleep apnea management. She has been using CPAP therapy but reports difficulty tolerating the treatment.

Physical Examination:
BMI 28.7 kg/m2.
No other significant findings noted.

Sleep Study and CPAP Data:
CPAP intolerance: download shows average use 3.2 hours per night on 38% of nights despite mask refitting; shared decision-making with the patient documented that CPAP is not tolerated.

Assessment:
The patient demonstrates suboptimal adherence to CPAP therapy due to intolerance despite efforts to optimize mask fit.

Plan:
Discuss alternative treatment options including oral appliance therapy and positional therapy.
Recommend follow-up sleep study if indicated.
Provide education and support for lifestyle modifications to improve sleep quality.

Follow-up:
Patient to return in 3 months or sooner if symptoms worsen or new concerns arise.

notes.author: Otolaryngologist
notes.text:
Otolaryngology Consultation Note
Date: 09/04/2026
Patient: Elvina Schaden, 69-year-old female

This 68-year-old woman referred for hypoglossal nerve stimulation evaluation. Drug-induced sleep endoscopy 08/28/2026: anteroposterior collapse at the velum without complete concentric collapse. Oropharynx: tonsils size 1, no other anatomic obstruction. No neuromuscular disease, hypoglossal palsy, severe cardiopulmonary disease or planned MRI; able to operate the sleep remote.

Given these findings and the absence of contraindications, the patient is a suitable candidate for hypoglossal nerve stimulation therapy. Further evaluation and planning will proceed accordingly.
